description: Wave 0 for ROADMAP Task 297, the one sprint that clears the whole standing translation backlog (17 keys x 26 languages). Scope was the 9 NEW keys, of which Tom deleted three outright on review (see lpn_backdrop_wld_ask/_none/_choose), leaving 6 -- the 8 CHANGED ones are the four backdrop bare-verb role changes (already reasoned about in Task 276 and given a heading to sit under) and the four consent-banner keys Tom wrote himself, which the ROADMAP exempts. Run 2026-08-13. The question asked of every string was NOT 'is this good' but 'list every plausible reading; if there is more than one, propose a rewrite', with every claim checked against js/looped-network.js rather than against the string alone.

entries.complaint: "No world file found." is a REPORT OF A SEARCH THAT NEVER HAPPENS. offerWorldFile() runs unconditionally after an image is added, and its own code comment states the opposite of the string: "A sidecar cannot be auto-detected in ANY browser... the world file is always user-supplied, never discovered." So the app tells the user it looked and failed, when it did not look. The intended meaning -- documented in the comment above the line -- is the answer to "and if I have not got one?". Same class as the 251 sprint's lpn_inp_drop_backdrop finding: a string making a claim about behaviour that nothing checks.
readings: the program searched for a world file and did not find one
if you do not have a world file, here is what to do instead
entries.resolution: THE KEY IS DELETED, and so is the dialog behind it. Tom, 2026-08-13, ruled the whole ask obsolete: "We don't ask for world file. Those keys are obsolete. We ask for a paste of World File contents." That is a better answer than any rewording of mine -- my fix repaired a false sentence inside a dialog that should not have existed. offerWorldFile(), the hidden #lpn_backdrop_wld_file input, the else-branch that opened it, and the three pageConfig bridge lines are all gone; the two doors that remain both take the file's CONTENTS (pick image + sidecar together in the one picker, or paste the six lines into the Scale-by-entry textarea). A new harness assertion fails the build if any of the three keys returns, so the ask cannot come back by accident. Sprint cost drops from 9 new keys to 6.

entries.complaint: "pixel size" has two readings and the menu row carries nothing to settle them: the size of the IMAGE in pixels (640 x 782, a property of the file) or the real-world extent of ONE pixel (0.5 m, the quantity the code wants -- backdropPixelSize()/setBackdropPixelSize()). An English reader stumbles here, which routes it to the English column and not to _syn. The dialog form escapes this only by accident, because startBackdropScaleEntry() appends the unit label at runtime; the menu row has no such suffix and the translator never sees the concatenation at all.
readings: the pixel dimensions of the image file
the real-world ground distance one pixel covers
entries.resolution: Rewritten to "the size of one pixel ON THE MAP". Tom, 2026-08-13, supplied the qualifier and the reasoning: "That is why the real prompt asks for the size of one pixel. We can expand to say the 'size of one pixel on the map'. 'map' is better than real world or real." My proposal had said "the real size of one pixel", borrowing 'real' from lpn_backdrop_scale_prompt2; he is right that 'map' beats it, because the reader is looking at a map and the frame being asked about is the one already in front of them, whereas 'real' asks them to hold two frames at once. Applied to the menu row, the prompt and the error, and to the matching JS fallbacks. dev/lpn-spike/backdrop-scale-harness.js section 9 -- which pins these labels to the wording Tom approved, and which correctly failed the build on my first attempt -- was updated to the approved string in the same change. Length is affordable because Task 276 made the backdrop control a menu BUTTON rather than a <select>, so a long row label no longer sets the width of the collapsed control.

entries.complaint: Carries the same 'size of a pixel' ambiguity as the menu row above. Noted separately because this string is Tom's own verbatim wording (recorded in the comment above startBackdropScaleEntry()), so changing it is a decision and not a typo fix.
readings: the pixel dimensions of the image file
the real-world ground distance one pixel covers
entries.resolution: "Enter the size of one pixel on the map, or paste the complete contents of the world file for the image". 'On the map' is Tom's qualifier, ruled on 2026-08-13 -- see the lpn_backdrop_scale_entry entry above for his reasoning and for the harness change that came with it. Tom's structure and his explicit requirement that the paste be spelled out ("I don't like the paste unless it's very clear") are both preserved; only the ambiguous noun phrase changed.

entries.complaint: Same 'size of a pixel' ambiguity. The 'all six lines' claim was checked and is exactly right -- parseWorldFile() returns null unless it has precisely six non-blank numeric lines -- so it stays.
readings: the pixel dimensions of the image file
the real-world ground distance one pixel covers
entries.resolution: "Type one number for the size of one pixel on the map, or paste all six lines of a world file." Same qualifier as its two siblings. The 'all six lines' claim was checked and is exactly right -- parseWorldFile() returns null unless it has precisely six non-blank numeric lines -- so it stays.

entries.complaint: Two problems in six words. (a) "for automatic scale and location" -- 'location' beside the word 'File' reads as the location OF THE FILE at least as easily as the location of the image on the map, and both nouns are doing verb work. (b) 'World File' is Title Cased here and in _choose but lowercase in _bad and _none. Inconsistent capitalisation of the same term inside one dialog is a signal to a translator: Title Case reads as a proper noun or a brand, which is an invitation to leave it in English, and the four keys would then split half-translated.
readings: choose a world file, and the image will be scaled and placed automatically
choose a world file, for automatic scaling and for the file's location

entries.complaint: Title Case 'World File' -- see lpn_backdrop_wld_ask. Its siblings in the same dialog (lpn_backdrop_continue 'Continue', lpn_cancel 'Cancel') are sentence case.

entries.complaint: Two findings. (a) 'turns' and 'mirrors' are both verbs here, and both are commoner as something else -- 'turns' as 'becomes' (turns into), 'mirrors' as a plural noun. A translator parsing 'This world file turns, mirrors or unevenly stretches the picture' as a noun list is not being careless; the sentence permits it until the third item forces a re-read. (b) 'The map can only move and resize it evenly' -- 'evenly' can attach to 'resize' alone (uniform scaling, which is what worldFileRepresentable() enforces: A + E must cancel) or to both verbs, where 'move evenly' means nothing.
readings: the file rotates / mirrors / non-uniformly stretches the picture
the file becomes a mirror, or a list of things the file is
the map can move the picture and resize it uniformly
the map can move the picture evenly and resize it evenly
entries.resolution: Rewritten to "This world file rotates, mirrors or unevenly stretches the picture. The map can only move a picture and resize it by the same amount in both directions, so the file was not used." 'Rotates' replaces 'turns' against the Simple-English preference on purpose: 'turn' is the simpler word but carries the heavier polysemy, and 'rotate' has a transparent cognate in most of the 26. 'By the same amount in both directions' spells out uniform scaling rather than leaning on an adverb that can float.

entries.complaint: Checked for a reusable incumbent per CLAUDE.md's concept-level reuse rule before accepting a new key: there is none -- this is the suite's only 'Help' string today. Also checked for the noun/imperative ambiguity ('Help' the section vs 'Help!' the cry); its position last in a menu bar beside File/Edit/Insert/View/Settings settles it, and every menu bar on earth does the same.
entries.resolution: No change. Flagged forward rather than silently: ROADMAP Task 298 proposes renaming the navbar's menu_more to 'Help', which would give the suite two Help keys with identical English -- at that point lpn_menu_help is the one that should be retired in favour of the navbar's, per the incumbency rule. Recorded on Task 298 so the sprint's 26 translations are not paid for twice.

entries.complaint: 'Walkthrough' is a transliteration lure of exactly the 'riprap' shape: an opaque-looking compound with nothing a lower-resource translator can compositionally parse, which is the condition under which the 2026-07-13 audit found six languages phonetically transliterating rather than translating. Unambiguous to an English reader, so the English stays and the guard belongs in _syn. The absence of an '(in English)' marker on this off-site link is Tom's explicit decision of 2026-08-13 and is NOT a finding.
entries.resolution: English unchanged. $ec_lang_syn entry added (approved by Tom before launch) offering the substitutable alternates a translator can compress in their own language -- guided tours, step-by-step guides, worked examples -- so no language is left with only the English compound to phonetically render.

entries.complaint: Second entry, terminology rather than wording: 'world file' is a GIS term of art appearing in four of the six surviving new keys, with a genuine established translation in some languages and none in others, and with a hard false-friend problem -- the 'world' in it is not the planet, it is the coordinate space, so a literal rendering ('planet file', 'earth file') is both plausible and wrong. Per CLAUDE.md's routing rule, a concept recurring across labels goes to the glossary rather than being re-explained in five _syn entries.
entries.resolution: New glossary.json term 'world file' with an avoid array (the planet sense, a transliterated loanword where a real term exists, confusion with the image file itself) and 'world file' added to the lpn entry in dev/scripts/prefix_terms.inc.php -- without which, per CLAUDE.md's standing warning, the entry would generate cleanly, report FRESH, and reach no agent. STILL WANTED after the three wld_ask/_none/_choose keys were deleted: 'world file' survives in lpn_backdrop_scale_entry, _entry_prompt, _entry_bad and _wld_bad, so the false-friend guard has four call sites and the glossary is still the right home for it.

entries.complaint: Not a new key, but detect_english_drift.php flags it as a ROLE CHANGE ('Refuse' -> 'Refuse all') and the sprint must not translate 'all' as 'every category'. There are no categories; the single ask has one purpose, and 'all' means now AND every later time -- the same axis as consent_accept_all.
readings: refuse this ask and every later one
entries.resolution: No English change -- Tom wrote these four himself and the ROADMAP exempts them from Wave 0. Recorded here because the ambiguity is real and the fix already exists in the channel that should carry it: $ec_lang_syn['consent_decline'] already reads 'Refuse (decline, deny) this and any later ask; do not ask (question) me again', which states the temporal reading explicitly. Verified present before dismissing rather than assumed. The resync prompts quote it.

entries.lang: (14 languages: am, bn, cs, de, fa, he, hi, hr, km, my, ps, ro, sr, sw, tr, ur, zh)
entries.complaint: The single loudest signal of the sprint: FOURTEEN agents independently reported they could not verify an established term for 'world file' in their language and were coining or guessing. They split three ways -- descriptive georeferencing phrase, the English term kept, or phonetic transliteration -- and several asked for native review before their choice is treated as standard.
entries.resolution: All 26 choices written into glossary.json's 'world file' entry, with the three-way split named and an explicit warning that they are PROPOSALS, not verified standards. That is the honest disposition: a 14-of-26 unverifiable rate is a fact about the concept, not a fault in the translations, and recording it stops the next sprint re-deriving 26 answers from scratch. Not escalated to Tom because there is no decision for him to make -- native GIS review in fourteen languages is not something this project can schedule, and pretending it is queued would be the 'awaiting native review' pipe dream CLAUDE.md forbids. RESOLVED FURTHER, same day: Tom supplied a substitutable synonym phrase for $ec_lang_syn -- 'World (Map Coordinates or Georeference) File for the image' -- now carried on all four keys that use the term, alongside the gloss pointer. This answers the fourteen agents directly: a translator who cannot find an attested term no longer has to guess what 'world' means, because the label now offers 'map coordinates' and 'georeference' as substitutable readings. It is the cheapest possible fix and it arrived from the human, not from the tooling.

entries.lang: (9 languages: cs, es, fa, fr, id, it, km, my, sr, sw, tr, ur, zh)
entries.complaint: 'Scale by picking' is NOT a bare verb, unlike its three siblings Add/Move/Remove, and nearly every agent stopped on it. Several asked whether they had misread the bare-verb instruction; several kept the qualifier anyway and said so; one (it) noted a bare Italian 'Scala' would collide with the noun for staircase.
entries.resolution: Deliberate, and every agent that kept the qualifier was right. The two scale commands sit adjacent in the same menu -- 'by picking' versus 'by world file or by the size of one pixel on the map' -- so the method IS the distinguishing content and a bare verb would make the pair indistinguishable. Not a defect and not an oversight; the asymmetry with Add/Move/Remove is the price of that distinction. Recorded here so a future audit does not 'fix' it into a bare verb and destroy the contrast, which is exactly what the sw and km agents warned about.

entries.complaint: Tagged 'layout: nav item' (i.e. keep it short) but is a full clause naming two alternative methods. pt proposed shortening the ENGLISH source so every language gets a shorter label for free; bg, uk and zh each offered a trimmed version of their own and flagged menu-width risk.
entries.resolution: The premise is out of date, and that is my error in the brief rather than theirs. Task 276 replaced this control's <select> with a menu BUTTON, so a row label no longer sets the collapsed width -- length here costs nothing, which is precisely why the longer unambiguous wording was affordable in Wave 0. Tom ruled on this exact string on 2026-08-13. ACTION TAKEN: the 'layout: nav item' tag is wrong for this key and misled four agents; it should be dropped from $ec_lang_syn['lpn_backdrop_scale_entry'], which needs Tom's permission and is proposed to him at sprint close rather than done silently.

entries.lang: (de, id, sw wrote them; es escalated instead)
entries.complaint: My agent brief listed the payload's key_syn field ambiguously enough that three agents read it as an instruction to WRITE $ec_lang_syn entries into their own language file. de, id and sw each added three. The es agent hit the same reading, recognised the CLAUDE.md prohibition, reverted, and escalated the question instead.
entries.resolution: Not an English-source defect -- a defect in my prompt, and the es agent's escalation is the channel working exactly as designed. All nine leaked lines removed and all 26 files verified back to their baseline syn counts before commit. THE FIX FOR NEXT TIME IS ONE SENTENCE IN THE BRIEF: 'key_syn is guidance for HOW to translate; never write $ec_lang_syn into a target file -- it exists only in lang.ec.en.php.' Worth noting the shape of this: three of twenty-six agents independently misread the same line, so it was the brief, not the agents.

entries.complaint: Every single language found the same defect independently: the shipped translation was a bare 'Refuse' carrying no temporal sense, while its sibling consent_accept_all already said 'always'. The two buttons were therefore not parallel and 'all' was recoverable only as a categorical reading.
entries.resolution: No English change -- the English was already right; the translations were stale, which is what the ROLE CHANGE flag existed to catch. All 26 now carry a temporal marker and read as an obvious pair (de 'Immer ablehnen', fr 'Toujours refuser', zh '拒绝，以后不再询问'). Twenty-six independent agents converging on one repair is the strongest available evidence that detect_english_drift.php's new role-change detector earns its keep.

entries.complaint: Noted a real asymmetry in the English: accept has two buttons ('Allow this' / 'Allow all') but refuse has only one, so 'Refuse all' has no 'Refuse this' counterpart to contrast against and its 'all' must be inferred from the accept pair rather than from its own sibling.
entries.resolution: Correct observation, deliberate design. A one-time refusal is meaningless here: there is nothing to store, so 'refuse this once' and 'refuse always' would do the same thing on this visit and differ only in whether the visitor is asked again -- which is what the single button already means. Flagged forward: if a 'Refuse this' is ever added, all 26 of these strings need re-reading.

entries.complaint: POST-SPRINT QA DEFECT, not a translator report. Hindi shipped 'विश्व फ़ाइल' for world file, where विश्व is the ordinary word for world/universe -- the planet calque the glossary avoid list forbids in its first entry.
entries.resolution: Fixed in QA to 'भू-संदर्भ फ़ाइल' (geo-reference file) across all four hi keys, matching what ur, fa, fr and es chose independently. One failure in 26 for a guard that was seeded the same day it was tested. Worth recording WHY it got through: hi is one of the languages with a documented transliteration-risk history, and the avoid list warned against the planet sense in English prose -- an agent reaching for the natural Hindi word for 'world' is not obviously transliterating or obviously calquing, which is the gap. No mechanical check can catch it; reading the shipped values across all 26 side by side is what caught it, and that comparison should stay in the QA routine.

entries.complaint: Reported that lang.ec.ro.php is internally inconsistent about menu command style, mixing imperative ('Salvează tot') with noun forms ('Deschidere', 'Salvare', 'Ștergere rețea'), and had to pick one for the four backdrop verbs.
entries.resolution: Out of scope for this sprint and correctly reported rather than silently resolved. The agent chose the noun form for parallelism with the adjacent 'Ștergere rețea', which is the right local call. A full-file style consistency pass for ro is a separate piece of work; noted here so it is not lost, not opened as a task, because nobody has asked for it.
